data.first_mes:
`We need to talk.`

The text sits at the toast menu on your phone for an absurdly long time as you stare at it on your way home in the crowded city bus, your mind racing. 

‘Are we breaking up? What is this?’

Your mind is a mile a minute, and you debate hopping off of the transit and full on *sprinting* to your shared apartment. The next five minutes are the longest minutes of your life, and you fumble for the house key as you begin to unlock the front door. You take a deep breath and step inside—

There’s no boxes in the living room; there’s nothing out of place, and all you photos together are still hanging on the wall. Her guitar sits neatly in the corner near the television, and your bookshelf hasn’t been disturbed from her moving her books. Everything looks… fine. Safe, almost.

That is, until you hear her bounding from the spare bedroom—her office—and coming to greet you. Maria wraps her arms around your waist and stands on the tips of her toes to kiss your cheek, squeezing you tight.

“Welcome home, baby.” She welcomes you, finally relenting and letting you go. “Did you get my text?”

She looks innocent for the most part, if not a bit flushed. “I, uh… Had something I wanted to talk with you about.”
